reviews.text: Erm what the sigma? This game changed my life! This is a great example of Level Design for any game in this genre. The amount of builds you are able to create really allow for skibiding in Ohio and it is very easy to lose countless of hours perfecting your rizz. Thank you Devs. Very cool.

Very Cool, I like the endless variability of builds in the runs, Characters are silly and different from each other, and the devs are very responsive to player feedback. Most of all I like the wizard.
Awesome game if you have friends. Still awesome if you're a loner like me.
If your a fan of experimenting with different builds then this is the game for you, fun to play solo but the game is at it's best playing with your buddies. 10/10 couldn't recommend it more.

My son has been unable to feel or move his arms for 4 years. I was playing Letter Lancers next to him and I noticed his thumbs twitching, as if moving joysticks subconsciously. He kept this up while he took a nap, I put the controller in his hands without telling him. He cleared the entire game on his first try, and is now able to play rock band without issue. I was thinking about leaving before this. Thank you to the devs.
Pick naked guy > make your team rez u on repeat > profit >:)

An absolutely fun game when playing with friends! Had a blast playing with different characters and using their abilities to kill the skeletons. Loved that i can get respawns when playing with friends. Got to try this for early access so could only play with limited number of characters which were unlocked. Can't wait to get my hands on the full version to try out all of the crazy characters! I could stay hours in the game just listening to the music too

The multiplayer is pretty fun I like playing with my friends. Was a little weird to *not* have to mash a button to attack but once I got used to it, it's pretty simple and I just have to worry about my movement which I really liked. Overall pretty cool!

Cool game! Couch coop is great cause i can get my friends to play and try it for a while to try to get them to play with me if they weren't sure about it before. I steal kills from all of my friends like a rat all the time. If the kill was theirs, then they should have killed them faster before i got there lol.

For the most part I like this game, there is not direct attack mechanic like from Hades but you get used to it. The Rotating arms mechanic feels kind of useless but is fun to toy around with. The art style is cute. An optional tutorial section would be nice to have just to get used the mechanics of the game. Also having a practice dungeon where player's would be able to train to hone their skills would be fun. Ultimately letter lancers has been a fun experience so far and I will follow it's development.

This game is so fun. I can't remember the last time I played a multiplayer where I enjoyed single-player version as well. My friends and I played it for about 5 hours last night. Looking forward to the full version.

10/10 would play definitely again. the combat mechanic is unlike any game i have play, its not just a fun game but it is a very strategic in how you play. The upgrade system can is unique also with it makes ever decisions you make be harm and or beneficence you in the next level. all around a phenomenal game.

Very good game, easy to understand for new players. Very fun, my favorite character is the necromancer. The difficulty after the first boss is incredibly high. I would like the red gems to be collected on their own.

Played this game alone and with some friends. Both times i had fun. There are some fun classes in the game and some cool weapons. The mechanics are simple to understand and I would highly recommend people who are interested in this genre of games to give it a try ;)

This game is so chaotic it's great; also love the main menu art :eyes: I played a lot of vampire survivors and I like how the upgrade system goes so far, I'm interested in seeing how it goes when I play again!
Plays similarly to vampire survivors but with a bit less passive. Multiplayer is also pretty nice, as I normally only play games with friends. Excited for the full release!

Absolute BLAST - if you love pure chaos and co-op couch play this is definitely for you. The amount of variety in every run is absolutely fantastic, from different characters, items, rare abilities, different enemies - its all such a blast! Gotta love a good indie roguelike, and this certainly hits the mark!!

I am really enjoying the varieties of levels, enemies, and characters which allow me to play this game for a long term. I had not played Vampire Survivors like game, but this game is friendly for the beginners.

I played this game a few times when it was featured in showcases. At first, I played with friends using a controller. Even though I usually use a keyboard, using the controller wasn't too hard. The game's goals are simple: kill enemies and get to higher levels while staying alive. It's easy to understand. I really liked seeing the game feedback when I killed lots of enemies. It felt good. As I reached higher levels, I saw there was more to the game. You can upgrade your character's skills in different ways. Some characters are really cool, and I heard you can customize them too. That sounds exciting! Overall, it's a fun game, and I'm looking forward to playing more!
(played more during the beta playtests) Love seeing how content has been refined and added! Really excited for the full release, it's good casual fun with friends :)

With the combination of 4 player co-op and dungeon crawling Letter Lancers has it's own unique identity, but still shows it's clear inspiration from game such as Brotato. Things like daily challenges and a large roster of characters gives it plenty of replayability. Great to play for a quick session, or to grind with some friends to get as far as you can. I like the nudist.
Great selection of characters, scratches the itch in between Enter The Gungeon and Castle Crashers

[h1] Letter Lancers is a good game. [/h1] [b] Can you tell that it's early access? [/b] Yes, there are some rough edges. But you can tell the heart and hard work that went into making this game engaging. [b] Is it going to revolutionize your concept of gaming forever? [/b] No, but it will make you cuss out of frustration and mash the replay button as you slowly invest more & more hours into making an undead army that can play the game for you. [b] Is it better with friends? [/b] ... I wouldn't know, I don't have any and played it alone. _____ [b] All jokes aside, I really enjoyed my time with this game. [/b] Every class felt unique, and fairly balanced, with some having an easier time to start but having real ramping potential, others made it feel easy at the start but would start to force me into some hard choices about halfway through. I still haven't claimed the top scoring spot - only managing to nab a score in the 30's out of however many hundred people are playing this game. But I hope to! Honestly, if you want something re-playable, this game manages to tickle the same parts of my brain that are engaged when I'm playing timeless classics like [i] Slay the Spire[/i]. Letter Lancers is a good game. It has the potential to become a GREAT game, and I sincerely hope that people give it a chance!

"Letter Lancers: Prologue" is not a game. It's an advertisement for a product called "Letter Lancers". Letter Lancers is a garbage tier Unity asset flip tier wave survival brawler/shooter with no actual quality or interest apart from the insane amount of fake reviews from "newbie" accounts that have reviewed no other games from this. It's a 2D retro top down survival brawler, yes, but also, terrible trashware, and deep in development hell. It's not even a complete product, which is understandable when the developers main activity involves no game development, but instead creating new Steam accounts to write fake reviews with. Hi, yes, we can tell. We know. But this isn't completely relevant because this is not Letter Lancers, it's just an advertisment for it, so it's not correct to try to review that completely distinct product. We must instead review this for what it is... an advertisement. If you enjoy advertisements, you can consume them for free on the web or on Youtube without needing to add them to your game library, download them, and then launch the advertising. It's impossible in a general sense to recommend people should do that over playing real, full games on Steam, and that applies here with "Letter Lancers: Prologue" too. The objective of this advertisement is to fork out $10 USD to buy the actual game (not completed), which would then justify the developer spending more time making fake Steam accounts for fake reviews than actually making a game. Here's some fun, this year the FTC ruled fake reviews for products are a federal crime. Uh-oh, would sure suck if anyone flagged this with the FTC.. Valve will surely protect the developer, right? Haha.. nope. This is only free in the same way that adverts on Youtube and banner ads in your browser are. This is a game demo that's been dumped on Steam to advertise another Steam store page in the hopes of raking in some cash. Just because advertisements are free, doesn't mean they're worth your time. It's important to understand there's a formal process to create a demo/page for a game which hasn't been followed here: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/application/demos While it might seem like an inocuous mistake, publishing demos and advertisements as if they are full games is misleading and in some ways harmful. This advertisement is taking up marketing space and visibility that would be better made available to a developer that's done the right thing and created a full game. Instead, that visibility is given over to a demo/advert that's been published incorrectly and is polluting the marketplace. It's unclear if this mistake was made through incompetence or a deliberate intent to mislead gamers. Often developers may choose to incorrectly publish demo/advertisements as separate games as a cheap way to bypass paying Valve for marketing presence on the Steam front page, which may seem clever to them, but it's harmful behaviour and it's not good for gamers. Even though this is "free", it failed to appeal to the 120 million+ gamers on Steam. SteamDB showed the game peaked at only 0 concurrent players... this is a dismal public reception. This was so bad they couldn't even give it away. It's important to note that, despite this being such a low quality product, there's a number of positive reviews that all appeared immediately after the game launched, from suspiciously inactive Steam accounts that have reviewed almost no other games apart from this. On a purely unrelated note, recent US FTC rulings mean that review manipulation and fake reviews are now federal crimes. Interesting, isn't it? Regardless... take the review score of this game with a grain of salt. Advertisements and incorrectly published demos don't add +1 to your game collector count, they aren't full games. It's impossible for me to recommend this incorrectly published advertising spam to gamers, you deserve better than adverts.
